extracted.intended_audience: readers and writers of literary essays and short stories (Spectator readership); aspiring storytellers interested in crafting entertaining/moral tales
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing short stories, fables, and conversational pieces that command attention and produce humour or moral effect, with emphasis on surprise, particulars, and stylistic graces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surprise as the life of stories
rubrics_metrics.description: “Surprize is so much the Life of Stories” — surprise is central to pleasing storytelling and to producing laughter or powerful emotional effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Smooth Delivery, an elegant Choice of Words, and a sweet Arrangement are beautifying graces, but they do not substitute for surprise; a story that lacks unexpected turns will not long command attention or produce the bursts of laughter or passion that constitute humour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Smooth delivery, elegant wording, and arrangement (style graces)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Smooth Delivery, an elegant Choice of Words, and a sweet Arrangement, are all beautifying Graces.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are important stylistic virtues that improve a story's surface and presentation, making it pleasant to read, but the author cautions that they alone will not secure lasting attention or the chief effects of humour without properly used surprise and striking particulars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use striking particulars (details) to sustain attention or provoke emotion
rubrics_metrics.description: Particulars in conversation or narrative should either "long command the Attention, or strike with the Violence of a sudden Passion, or occasion the burst of Laughter which accompanies Humour."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select concrete, vivid incidents or details that either sustain interest over time or deliver a sharp, unexpected impact. Focus on particulars that can produce prolonged focus or a sudden comic/passionate reaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make the moral of a fable clear and practically relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: When using a fable to illustrate a point (e.g., about Hope), the essayist insists on deriving a clear moral: do not entertain hopes for things at a great distance; weigh the object and likelihood of attainment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design fables so that their incident directly embodies the abstract precept you wish to teach. The example (Alnaschar) is used to demonstrate how visionary hopes lead to ruin — the fable should therefore be simple, natural, and obviously tied to the lesson.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a concrete illustrative story to embody abstract reflection
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstract reflections (on hope, virtue, dignity of human nature, etc.) are best served by being exemplified with a short, lively tale (the Arabian Fable is given as such an example).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer a brief, engaging narrative with a clear, resonant image that readers can relate to; the tale should be simple, naturally told, and capable of prompting reader self-recognition of the vice or virtue under discussion.
